steps.content: The courtroom is solemn and imposing. Everyone lowers their face instinctively in the face of the dark seats and cavernous dome.
The gallery is packed. There are jury members, reporters, and professors from the School of Forensic Science here. Even the families of the victims are present.
This isn't your first time attending a trial, but it is the first time you're appearing as both plaintiff and witness.
To expedite evidence collection and fast-track the trial proceedings, you pulled some strings as the MBCC Chief.
It isn't exactly by the book, but just as Forensica said—rules bend for those in power.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: Order! Court is now in session. Bring in the defendant, Aster Wynne!
The Origami Killer is dressed in ordinary clothes. Her face is pale and gaunt, bearing the sickly pallor one would find in patients with chronic illness.
She displays a perfect look of bewilderment, placing her right hand over her chest as she acknowledges the judge and jury.
She appears to be someone highly skilled at deception and exploiting the system. It's no wonder Forensica's investigation kept hitting dead ends.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: Defendant Aster Wynne, how do you plead?

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: Your Honor, I cannot enter a plea. I was arrested without warning in my own home and brought to this court without even being informed of the charges against me.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: Or is evidence and arrest warrants simply not required in DisCity? The citizens here can be arbitrarily detained, just like this?

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: I was expelled from the Forensic Association years ago. The little money I managed to scrape together from odd jobs barely covers my medical bills. Where would I possibly find the time or energy to commit crimes?
Aster coughs twice, perfectly timed. The jury members exchange uneasy glances and murmur among themselves. The judge's expression darkens.

This trial was rushed, and you were the one who forced it forward. Most details of the case remain unclear, which has drawn considerable criticism from the prosecution already. If you fail to uncover the truth here, your reputation will suffer as well.
Aster's eyes sweep across the courtroom before settling on you. For a brief moment, her expression shifts. It's subtle, yet she's unmistakably mocking you.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: The prosecution may proceed.

Your Honor, members of the jury. We are not here today to discuss a simple murder case. We are here to expose a years-long, meticulously planned criminal conspiracy. The defendant, Aster Wynne, has used her expertise as a forensic pathologist to commit a series of perfect murders.

Ms. Wynne was expelled jointly by DisCity University's School of Forensic Science and the Forensic Association. The official reason cited was misconduct, but according to our investigation, the truth is that she lacks basic respect for human life and has repeatedly violated professional ethical standards.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: This is slander against my character. I was expelled due to certain... misunderstandings at the time.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: Furthermore, administrative sanctions cannot constitute direct evidence of murder. This is nothing but defamation.
I must ask you to refrain from interrupting. You will have ample opportunity to respond after I've finished presenting my case.
And given how much you'll need to refute, would you like me to provide you with paper so that you may take notes?
Then again, as a top graduate of DisCity University's School of Forensic Science, I'm sure you can manage without.
It seems you've picked up Forensica's habit of speaking without knowing it—your words are laced with sarcasm.
It certainly is satisfying though, being able to make someone squirm while you remain perfectly composed.
Aster seems to notice this as well. Her expression shifts briefly, and she glances around the room, carefully and subtly, as though searching for someone.
She presses her right hand to her chest, perhaps because she's struggling to withstand such verbal assault. Her expression takes on one of wounded grievance.

Shortly after your expulsion, the first Origami Killer case occurred. Since then, at regular intervals, cases with identical methods would arise—victims would seemingly die by suicide or accident, but every scene would be marked by a single origami flower.

options: Show case files and autopsy report

steps.content: We noticed special paper fibers from the throat tissue samples of the most recent victim. Laboratory analysis confirms they're identical to fiber samples extracted from the throats of previous victims.
These fibers originate from specialized recording paper used exclusively by the School of Forensic Science.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: Plenty of people have access to that paper. That includes students, instructors, and even janitors at the department.
But not everyone would know how to weaponize it for murder.
Your movements were discreet, I'll admit. But you still left a trail.

options: Show the investigation report on Aster Wynne

steps.content: This is a report documenting your movements over the past few years, including everyone you've contacted and every location you've visited.
Cross-referencing this data with the times and locations of the Origami Killer's crimes yields an overlap rate of nearly one hundred percent.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: Is screening big data what you call an "investigation" here? And I just happened to be the poor soul who got flagged as the killer?
We didn't need to screen anything to obtain this data. If anything, I don't understand why no one thought to cross-reference it until now.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: With all due respect, as a former forensic pathologist, I wouldn't even classify this as evidence.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: You're... the MBCC Chief, correct? Perhaps you should focus on what you actually do best instead.
A textbook deflection. I must be on the right track.
There's no need to rush. The key evidence will be submitted by another witness. I'm just here to present what I need to.
Based on the investigative findings, I charge the defendant with the following crimes—
First, the murder of at least seven victims. The modus operandi demonstrates a high degree of consistency with distinctive characteristics. This series of crimes has been classified as serial murder.

Second, following the commission of said murders, the defendant deliberately left origami flowers at each scene as both a provocation and a signature. Furthermore, utilizing their expert knowledge of forensic examination procedures and evidentiary protocols, the defendant systematically misdirected investigations by staging scenes to resemble suicides or accidental deaths, thereby obstructing justice, impeding investigation, and demonstrating contempt for the law.

Third, during the investigation of the Eligy case, the defendant exploited professional connections to illegally obtain private information about the victim's family. She then coerced the family members into withdrawing their report and refusing an autopsy, substantially perverting the course of justice and causing the case to remain misclassified for years.

As you finish speaking, the courtroom falls into a heavy silence. But even under the watchful eyes of the jury, as well as the forensic academy's faculty and students, Aster remains completely composed.
The killer possesses an iron will. Her expression remains unchanged. If anything, she seems to be wearing a faint, sardonic smile.
I request permission to call our witness.
The judge nods in approval. The side door opens, and Forensica's figure appears behind it.
Aster's smile freezes. But a moment later, a genuinely pleased expression crosses her face.
Unlike the mere curiosity of the others, she gazes at Forensica with an almost fanatical intensity.

steps.speaker: Judge
steps.content: Please state your identity for the record. You are Foren—

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Forensica. Former member of the Forensic Association... and a Sinner of the MBCC.
Forensica cuts off the judge and introduces herself. You didn't expect her to introduce herself like that, and you meet her eyes in surprise.
Does this mean that regardless of how the trial ends, she's willing to go under the supervision of the MBCC?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Long time no see, senior.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: I'm glad to hear you call me that. Of all my juniors, you were always the one I had the highest hopes for.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: And I'm equally glad to see you standing in the defendant's dock.
Forensica's gaze locks onto Aster. She doesn't blink, as if the slightest lapse in attention might allow Aster to slip away.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: The paper balls puzzled me for the longest time. I couldn't figure out what kind of killer would be so obsessed with them.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: A novelist who works with words? A courier who delivers documents? A factory worker who makes paper, or perhaps someone who recycles it?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: I was so fixated on the paper that I lost sight of the murders themselves.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Being able to disguise the true cause of death using so many different methods—that in itself is a display of expertise.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: The person I was up against wasn't some cunning criminal. It was a forensic pathologist with the same level of expertise as mine.
Aster seems almost... pleased to see such a look from Forensica. She even smiles as she responds.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: I appreciate the recognition, truly. But I can't confess to something I didn't do.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: By that logic, any forensic pathologist could be a suspect.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: I went back to the school and examined all the forensic notes. Including yours.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Your notes were exemplary. They've always been used as reference material.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: But there was something I noticed—some of the pages weren't quite flat. They looked like they'd been folded and smoothed out again, and they were stained with unidentified tissue fluid.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Nearly every forensic pathologist is a perfectionist. They prefer clean, flat paper, and if their notes get stained during documentation, they're bound to make another copy.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: But you didn't do that. You left those creases and stains on the pages. That's because to you, they weren't imperfections. They were proof of your success.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: Success? Perfectionist? My, I didn't expect you, out of all people, to stereotype our profession like that. And what exactly does this prove? That I'm a sloppy pathologist who doesn't mind a few wrinkles?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Murdering someone through suffocation by paper ball—that couldn't have been perfected on the first try, could it?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: The size of the paper ball, the duration of suffocation, how to insert it precisely, and how to remove it completely intact...

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: You must have spent a long time trying to perfect all of that. Those creases and stains are proof of this.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Those seemingly random scribbles on the pages? They're the data from every "experiment" you've conducted.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: All I hear are speculations. Where's your evidence?

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: Surely you don't intend to convict me based on nothing but subjective theories?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Of course not. The evidence is on you.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: It's being kept in the pocket at your chest, to be precise.
The bailiffs exchange a glance before quickly restraining Aster's hands and retrieving a small notebook from said pocket.
The notebook reeks of disinfectant and formalin, but even that cannot mask the underlying stench of decay.
The gloved examiner opens the notebook. The pages inside are secured with ring fasteners and, just as Forensica said, bear jagged creases and stains.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: I kept wondering where those paper balls used in the murders ended up.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: If the killer wanted to commit the perfect crime, they would have destroyed the paper balls.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: But the killer was confident that the true cause of death would never be discovered. And so, these paper balls became more than just murder weapons—they became trophies. Medals of victory.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: That's why you kept them so close to your body. Isn't that right?
The stains on the notebook only need to be tested, and one will be able to see whether they match the victims' DNA.
The murder weapon, the method, and the movement patterns presented earlier—all of it forms an irrefutable chain of evidence.
Aster takes a deep breath. Her expression contorts, becoming a volatile mix of excitement, frustration, anger, and disappointment.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: ...I didn't expect you to find me this fast.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: It shouldn't have been like this...

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: You lost power, just like I did. You should've been scrambling through all the little traps I laid out, desperate, frantic. You should've been sneaking around for scraps of evidence still, catching glimpses of hope only to watch them slip away, over and over again.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: And just when you'd start doubting yourself, I'd appear to reveal the truth—proclaiming to the world that I alone am the victor!

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: Or... you'd catch me making a mistake, take me prisoner, and then... you'd become the next me!

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: That's impossible. I would never doubt myself.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: I'm the best forensic pathologist there is. The best.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Period.
She'd never become someone like you, either.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: Is that so? Hehe... But I've already achieved half of my goals... or it might be more accurate to say that I've already won.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: You and I are the same. What you hate most are those meaningless rules, and all that social decorum.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: You caught me, sure. So what?

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: Did you not utilize what you despise most to get here? Authority that oversteps its bounds, an institution that shields wrongdoing?

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: The dead can't be brought back to life. The institutional credibility you've put your faith in is worthless. What good is truth when it comes too late?

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: Did you think you'd be able to restore your status as a forensic pathologist? Or maybe you just wanted to savor the taste of victory?

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: My dear junior... you're just satisfying your own desires. You're just like me.
Forensica stands behind the witness stand, her lips pressed into a tight line, face drained of color. She offers no response.
I'll repeat myself again—she'd never become someone like you.
The rules, the authority, and the public trust you claim to despise... those are the very things you relied on.
Whether you realized it or not, when you conducted those experiments, indulging your desires and selfishness, you were relying on authority.

This world functions because of these things you hate so much. The difference is that some use these things to corrupt the world, while others wield them with conviction to pursue happiness and justice.
The judge strikes the gavel and delivers the verdict. Bailiffs escort Aster into custody, but this is not the end of the case. It is only the beginning.
The full extent of Aster's crimes has yet to be revealed. Many details still need to be uncovered, and some victims have yet to be found.
As she's being brought away, she passes by Forensica. A condescending smile crosses her face then.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: How does it feel? Being the one to wield authority and manufacture your truth for once?

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: I knew you'd find me eventually, but I didn't think you'd do it this way.

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: So tell me—how does it feel to defeat me with what you despise most?

steps.speaker: Aster
steps.content: Would you have ever made it this far if it weren't for your dear Chief here?
You glance at Forensica with concern. To your surprise, her expression remains stern and composed. Aster's provocations didn't get to her.
But she doesn't respond either. She simply turns and walks away in silence.
Outside the Courthouse, After the Trial
The sky is overcast. The air is dry and cold. Forensica stands on the steps in front of the courthouse, gazing up at the gray, hazy sky.
The cold wind tousles her hair. Forensica closes her eyes, as though a pair of icy hands were brushing across her face.
You walk over to her side, wanting to offer some words of comfort, but you are not sure where to start.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: The day Eligy was buried... it was a winter day just like this.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: By then, I'd already been fired from the institution. Her family even filed a restraining order against me. All I could do was watch from a distance as they lowered that black coffin into the ground... and all the evidence destroyed with it.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: That was the closest I ever got to the killer. If only I could have proven she was murdered back then... I could have linked her case to the Origami Killer.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: She was the first victim of the Origami Killer I ever encountered. If I had been allowed to perform an autopsy, I know I could've found the true cause of death.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: But the institution just kept delaying and rejecting my requests. They said Eligy's family cared too much about their reputation to allow for an autopsy. The Origami Killer had also lain low for years by then, so it could've just been a copycat or a coincidence. On top of that, serial killings cause public panic, and there wasn't enough evidence to link the cases together either.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: They were blind. Or rather, turned a blind eye. They refused to see that paper flower for what it was.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Reputation. Rules. Public opinion. To them, all of that mattered more than the life of a human.
But you did it in the end.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Yes. With your help, I did.
No, you simply used me well.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Do you know why I was so obsessed with this case?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Because on the day Eligy was buried, the killer walked right past me... and slipped an origami flower into my pocket.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: She chose me as her opponent. As her toy.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: At first, maybe it really was just about winning. But after risking my life countless times for the investigation... I started to lose sight of what I was fighting for.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: It's just like Aster said... I despise rules and power, yet I used them to convict her.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Just like how she used the same things to cover up the truth and deceive me... we're no different.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: That's... Eligy's toe tag!? You actually got it back...
This is the toe tag they found on you when you were arrested. I had to work pretty hard to convince them you weren't some kind of deranged creep.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: I owe you for this one. Aster really was right. I couldn't have caught her without you.
Without you, I couldn't have caught her either.
Forensica has carried Eligy's toe tag around all these years, constantly reminding her not to forget she must find the truth for that dead girl. It wasn't just about winning. It was about justice.
You're not like Aster. You never wanted to win. You just wanted the truth.
Power can become unbalanced, trust can be betrayed, and justice can be delayed. There's no such thing as "perfect justice" in this world, just as there's no such thing as a perfect crime.
But reverence for life remains constant. Doesn't matter what the methods used were or the outcome achieved.
Using rules, breaking rules, wielding power, resisting power—there's no right or wrong in any of these actions. What matters is your will.
Forensica slips the toe tag back into her pocket and smiles at you. A genuine, simple smile.
She pulls her clothes tighter around herself, turns, and starts descending the steps. But then, she suddenly stops.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Your Bureau handles some pretty complex cases, doesn't it? You're bound to need a forensic pathologist. How about it? Will you consider me?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: I might not have an official license anymore, but my skills are still unmatched.
Under normal circumstances, I couldn't accept someone without a license.
But it'd be a different story if I was simply engaging in professional collaboration with a technical consultant.
The air remains cold. Wind sweeps across your faces, then across the world beyond. The earth is frozen, but it is also clean.
